study.question: Can history-conditioned auxiliary tower representations improve click prediction through a detached forward edge beyond a matched receiver-self readout, and does learned auxiliary item representation alter that benefit?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: g3-r0005-private_aux_items reached click AUC 0.6601638278 and auxiliary AUCs 0.8484901/0.8659023/0.8686655, whereas g3-r0005-fixed_aux_items reached click 0.6604035937 but auxiliaries 0.6103671/0.6853433/0.5569850. Thus private item learning restores auxiliary prediction without a demonstrated click gain; the fixed-table selection winner has a large secondary-task cost. Mechanism hypothesis: auxiliary-owned representations contain complementary target/history information that click can read without sending click gradients into those representations. Trajectory review: initial task/feedback routing alone did not improve baseline-din (0.6555441); primary-only selector learning improved it (g3-r0001-primary_feedback 0.6576086). Additional detached/live auxiliary selectors (0.6574206/0.6567847) lost to g3-r0002-wide_primary (0.6583679). Blocking auxiliary item updates improved click (g3-r0003-embedding_item_primary 0.6601634), while nonzero gradient scales 0.1/0.5 and global auxiliary-loss attenuation failed to exceed it (0.6596625/0.6593366/0.6594593). The tied-primary r0005 control exactly reproduced 0.660163362657485; private item adaptation was effectively null for click at that seed. These successful executions with null/negative contrasts are retained; no execution failure was supplied in the authorized trajectory. No gradient-conflict diagnostic or seed uncertainty is available, so negative-transfer explanations remain provisional.

nearest_work.difference: STEM already combines shared/task-specific embeddings with cross-task forward access and stopped gradients into other task experts. We adapt that established principle to one-way auxiliary-to-click transfer after history pooling, retaining grouped auxiliary item tables and the primary-owned selector. No general novelty or exact reproduction claim.

AITM transfers tower-level vectors along a sequential conversion path and calibrates ordered probabilities. We read auxiliary tower vectors in parallel into click, stop donor gradients, and assume no label nesting or conversion order; category/brand matched auxiliary labels do not justify those constraints.

DIN supplies target-conditioned local activation and Dice; those are inherited from the field/four-task adaptation. The donor residual and gradient ownership experiment are added, without claiming exact original DIN reproduction.

INFNet mixes categorical, sequence and task representations through proxies and gated blocks. Its pinned benchmark source and primary methodology were inspected; this experiment instead tests a single late donor edge, not proxy aggregation or an INFNet implementation.

Closest empirical parent; exact archived SHA256 ce37e19401ecf4655df41d2797787c074b878646dfe837099d541f53d30445ff verified locally. Preserve constructor initialization and all inherited hidden computations; append only a zero-initialized residual adapter and expose existing penultimate states.

inherited_components: Pinned FeatureEmbeddingDict and MultiTaskModel input filtering; allowed user/context/target/history fields only
Primary-owned 128/32 Dice history selector and task-specific readout rows; feedback remains in score inputs
Private auxiliary item/action tables cloned exactly after parent reset, shared across three auxiliary tasks; shared user/context embeddings
All four 128/64 Dice towers and prediction readouts; sum of unweighted four BCEs; no custom loss hook
History mask applied before Dice statistics and pooling; target action never consumed; no timestamp or sample-index access
study.proposed_difference: Expose each inherited tower penultimate state with one execution of its existing modules. Concatenate either the three detached auxiliary states or three copies of the detached click state. Apply one new bias-free matrix W[64,192] initialized to zero without RNG draws, and add its output to the click penultimate state before the inherited final linear classifier. Only click learns W. Cross this donor-source replacement with learned versus fixed auxiliary item/action tables to obtain a complete 2x2. All variants are standalone modules; default/CONFIG switches are identical to proposal configs. No new embedding tables beyond the parent, no new labels, no pretraining and no changed host recipe.
predictions: At initialization, zero residual preserves the corresponding archived parent probabilities for all four tasks, and the additional parameter construction leaves the parent RNG stream unchanged. This is a source-derived invariant awaiting host verification, not a measured reproduction.

If learned donor information helps, learned_aux_transfer should improve full-validation click AUC over learned_self_transfer; auxiliary mean AUC and each task Logloss should remain near the learned parent rather than the fixed-table collapse.

If learned item adaptation contributes to complementary information, the predeclared click-AUC interaction should be positive; otherwise learned donor specificity is unsupported even if both auxiliary-donor cells improve.

At a fixed parameter state, backpropagating click alone has no gradient through the detached donor states into auxiliary towers/private tables; backpropagating auxiliary losses still trains their own towers, score rows, learned private tables and shared context. Indirect changes through shared context and clipping remain possible.

Report full-population click AUC/Logloss for selection, all task AUC/Logloss, auxiliary mean separately, allocated/trainable parameters, GPU/wall seconds, examples, peak memory, throughput and batch latency. Report only host-provided slices with sample/positive/negative counts: negatives are samples minus positives. Existing 0/1-16/17-64/>64 history bins are predeclared; other unavailable slices must be marked unavailable rather than fabricated.
falsifiers: Learned auxiliary donors fail to exceed the matched learned self-donor control: no evidence that this particular transfer edge adds complementary task information under the frozen one-pass recipe.
The learned-versus-fixed interaction is zero or negative: no support that auxiliary item adaptation specifically improves transfer over the receiver-self replacement.

Any initialization mismatch, duplicated Dice update, padding/current-action dependence, nonfinite probability/loss/gradient, missing task output or forbidden-input use invalidates interpretation and requires correction before performance comparison.
Auxiliary quality collapses toward the fixed-table baseline or click improves only by trading away secondary tasks: report that tradeoff and reject the claimed joint benefit.

A benefit disappears under paired repetitions or a stronger receiver/donor semantic control: revise the mechanism explanation. This suite does not test the necessity of stop-gradient, because there is no live-donor cell.
alternative_explanations: Only the protocol seed is scheduled in this round; observed differences are preliminary until paired-seed repetition.

Receiver-self input repeats one 64-dimensional state three times; auxiliary donor input has up to 192 distinct dimensions. Allocated/active parameter counts and dense multiply sizes match, but effective input rank and optimization geometry do not.

Context embeddings remain jointly trained, the primary selector conditions all histories, and host dense clipping can couple updates. Stop-gradient blocks the explicit donor edge only; this is not full task isolation.
Auxiliary representations evolve online in a single pass; early untrained donors or the late linear adapter can fail even if a richer or delayed transfer mechanism would succeed.
A residual adapter may improve conditioning, calibration or optimization without useful auxiliary semantics; the active receiver-self replacement is included for this reason.

Learnt auxiliary and primary features may be correlated or redundant; positive transfer can reflect generic extra input rank rather than task-label-specific knowledge. No novelty or causality claim beyond the tested contrasts.

The auxiliaries are user/category/brand matches in a 24h window, not ad-specific downstream events. The inherited official_offline feedback visibility and whole-window/static snapshots limit inference to this benchmark.
